question: Can two fund managers and one adjacent reporting interval separate stock redemption exposure from manager ownership, and what quantity comparison is observable?
inputs: complete original semiannual and annual fund reports; first public announcement dates; existing price source metadata only
flow_definition: (H2 redeemed units - H2 subscribed units) / beginning H2 units; H2 gross flows = FY gross - H1 gross; cannot label net cash or forced selling
simple_opponent: fund ownership proportions at interval start; with two funds one interval pressure is exactly affine in ownership fraction
core: reconcile all original holding totals and unit bridges; compute initial union/intersection and end/entry/exit; algebraic identifiability check, not return test
optional_comparison: for securities present at all four fund-date observations, log((end_shares_A/start_shares_A)/(end_shares_B/start_shares_B)); common proportional mandatory share changes cancel; differential corporate events and intentions remain unqualified
scope_limit: two selected existing products, no generalization to all funds or ETF/account effectiveness
stop_condition: this one-interval signal is mathematically redundant with same-date ownership, so no IC or return fitting is warranted; finish qualification and observable mechanism comparison
reopen_condition: same historical funds over varying flow dates with both flow directions and qualified lagged holdings, cash buffer and corporate-event identity; or independent contemporaneous forced-sale evidence; explain incremental identifying information before expansion
new_entry: external fund report qualification outside native technical feature runner; no claim of native workflow acceptance
